verdicts.summary: If the promote-to-steer guard rejects the steer, the queued run's cancel events are thrown away with the failed command, so the queued run stays queued and held.
verdicts.scenario: Stop with holdQueue sets queueHeld on the queued run. Then promote-to-steer runs. The promote handler emits cancelled run, attempt and node events into the events Ref (7770-7809) before dispatchSteerIntoRun fails at 3963. I checked whether those cancel events still get persisted. They do not: the error propagates out of the switch at 11141 before events are collected at 11244.

verdicts.summary: After a Stop with holdQueue, an auto send now queues behind the still-running run, and because the user sent it, the held queue is released. Stop sets the hold when it is requested, not when the provider finishes stopping, so the new run does not get re-held afterwards.
verdicts.scenario: Steps: Stop with holdQueue:true, then the user sends an auto message from the web client, then the provider later reports the stop. I checked whether any code applies queueHeld when the provider stop finishes, which would leave the new message stuck. holdStoppedThread runs only inside the interrupt command (9314) and holds only the runs that are queued at that moment (8961-8968). The re-hold at 1340-1360 fires only for a failed or missing provider, not for a user stop. The new run is queued because the stopping run still counts as blocking (5007), and it is created without queueHeld because heldRunsToRelease is non-empty (5173).
